newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: MINISTER SAYS THERE'LL BE NO CONFLICT OF INTEREST
Primary Industries Minister John Anderson says he'll make sure there can be no questions of conflict of interest raised about him when grain growers take control of the wheat industry fund.
Under a proposal endorsed by grain growers, the Fund would become a capital trust with growers owning shares.
As a grower, Mr Anderson will be entitled to shares, but he says he'll be careful about his conduct.
AUSTRALIAN ROADS BECOMING MORE CROWDED
If you think Australia's roads are getting more crowded, official figures show you're right.
The Australian Bureau of Statistics says a survey, conducted last year, shows there are almost 11 million motor vehicles in the nation. That's a rise of around one million on the 1991 survey figures.
Queensland vehicles travel the highest average distance annually ... 17,100 kilometres.
Vehicles in Tasmania record the lowest distance..13 and a half thousand kilometres.
NEW CHOPPER FACILITY AT OAKEY
About 250 army personnel and at least as many dependants will move to Queensland's Darling Downs, following the signing of a treaty by the Australian and Singaporean Governments.
The signing of the treaty means a new helicopter training facility will be built at the oakey Army Aviation Centre, with a squadron of 12 Super Puma helicopters to be based there.
Local Federal member, Liberal Bill Taylor says Australian companies will build the facilities and service the choppers.
ARMED MAN HOLDS THREE CHIDREN HOSTAGE
Police are negotiating with a man who's holding three children hostage in a home south of Brisbane.
Police have cordoned off a street at Shailer Park where police believe a shot was fired.
Police are directing traffic around a section of Bryants Road while negotiators try to talk the man into surrendering.
Logan detective inspector Chris Furlong says the man, aged in his early thirties, locked himself inside his unit about two hours ago.
GAMBLING TRIP KEEPS MURDERER BEHIND BARS
A trip to the Sydney Casino has seen a convicted murderer lose his chance of freedom.
Peter Schneidas was found to have breached conditions of his work release program when he was caught gambling and begging at the casino this month.
He was due to appear before the parole board but he's now in maximum security at Long Bail Jail and will go before the Offender's Review Board instead.
Schneidas, 39, was sentenced to life for the 1989 murder of a prison guard, while he was serving a 15-year sentence for false pretences.
GAYS AND LESBIANS MORE LIKELY TO BE BASHED IN SYDNEY
A study by NSW Police has shown lesbians are 6 times more likely to be physically assaulted than other women in Sydney.
It also showed gays in Sydney are four times more likely to be subject to attack than other men.
The level of violence against the homosexual community has prompted a campaign, called Homophobia: What Are You Scared Of?, launched today by NSW Attorney General Jeff Shaw.
MYSTERIOUS CLOUD SPOTTED IN CENTRAL AUSTRALIA

Several residents in the Central Australian town of Yulara have reported seeing a large grey circular cloud around the sun. One resident says the cloud looks like something out of the recent alien invaders movie, "Independence Day".
But the Weather Bureau says the phenomenon is nothing to be concerned about. It says the effect is caused by sunlight passing through high-level ice particles.
A spokesperson says the particles split the light into its component colours, creating the ring-like effect. A similar phenomenon occurred over Alice Springs two years ago.
